seoTitle: How to Recover Your Hostinger Account Without Email
metaDescription: Learn how to recover a Hostinger account when you've lost access to your registered email, including identity verification and contacting support.
intro: Losing access to the inbox tied to your Hostinger account is one of the more panic-inducing login problems, because the usual "forgot password" link just sends a reset email you can no longer read. Hostinger anticipated this and built a separate recovery flow specifically for lost or dead email addresses, rather than leaving you stuck. This guide walks through where that option actually lives on the login screen, what the recovery form asks for, and how to fall back on human support if the automated path stalls. It's aimed at anyone locked out because an old email was deleted, forgotten, or abandoned.

steps.heading: Find the "Can't Access Your Account?" link
steps.body: On the standard Hostinger login page, underneath the Email address and Password fields, there's a "Forgot password?" link right below the password box — but that's not what you want if the email itself is the problem. Scroll past the main Log in button and you'll see a second link, "Can't Access Your Account?", sitting on its own beneath the login form. That's the entry point for this whole recovery flow, and it's easy to miss because it looks secondary to the password reset option above it.

image.caption: The standard Hostinger login screen. The recovery flow starts from "Can't Access Your Account?", not the password reset link above the Log in button.

steps.heading: Open Account recovery and pick your scenario
steps.body: Clicking that link lands you on a dedicated Account recovery page with three radio-button options: Lost Two-Factor Authentication, Lost Access To Email, and Forgot Email. If you still know your email address but simply can't receive messages there anymore, select Lost Access To Email. If you've forgotten the email address itself, choose Forgot Email instead — the two lead to different verification questions, so picking the right one up front saves a wasted attempt.

image.caption: The Account recovery screen, with Lost Two-Factor Authentication, Lost Access To Email, and Forgot Email listed as separate recovery paths.

steps.heading: Enter the account email and submit
steps.body: Below the three options is an Account Email field with a note reading "Enter the email address associated with your account." Type in the address on file even if you can no longer log into it — Hostinger uses this to look up the account, not to send you something you'd need to open. Once filled in, click Start Account Recovery to move to the identity-verification step.

steps.heading: Verify your identity with domain or payment proof
steps.body: Because there's no working inbox to confirm you're the account owner, Hostinger asks for other evidence instead — details tied to a domain registered on the account, or information from a past payment such as the card's last digits or an order date. Have this on hand before you start the form, since gathering it mid-flow after a timeout is a common source of frustration. The more specific and accurate the details you provide, the faster this step clears.

steps.heading: Escalate to Hostinger support if automated recovery fails
steps.body: If the self-service flow can't confirm your identity from the details you provide, it will point you to Hostinger's live support instead of leaving you stuck. Reach out through the in-app chat or support ticket system and explain that you've already tried the Account recovery form — this saves the agent from re-explaining the same steps and gets you straight to manual verification, which can involve additional documentation for higher-value accounts.

steps.heading: Update your registered email once you're back in
steps.body: The moment you regain access, go to your account settings and replace the old email with one you control and check regularly. Skipping this step is how people end up back at square one a year later, having forgotten the same dead inbox was still on file. It only takes a minute and closes the loop on the whole recovery process.

faq.question: What if I no longer have access to the email on my Hostinger account?
faq.answer: Use the "Can't Access Your Account?" link on the login page, choose Lost Access To Email or Forgot Email on the Account recovery screen, and verify your identity with domain or payment proof instead of an email confirmation.

faq.question: How long does Hostinger account recovery take?
faq.answer: The self-service form can resolve in minutes if your verification details match. If it escalates to support for manual review, expect it to take longer, especially if extra documentation is requested.

faq.question: What proof does Hostinger accept for identity verification?
faq.answer: Details like a domain registered on the account or specifics from a past payment (such as the last digits of a card or an order date) are typically used to confirm ownership when email confirmation isn't possible.

faq.question: What's the difference between "Lost Access To Email" and "Forgot Email"?
faq.answer: Lost Access To Email is for when you know the address but can't receive messages there. Forgot Email is for when you don't remember the address itself. They're separate options on the same Account recovery page.

faq.question: Should I update my email after recovering my account?
faq.answer: Yes — as soon as you're back in, replace the old address with one you actively use so the same lockout doesn't happen again.
